PR surface: Source +16, Tests +73. Total +89 across 2 files.

target.title: fix(openai): reject malformed Codex image base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users generating images through the OpenAI Codex Responses route could receive truncated or corrupted image bytes when an SSE response contained malformed Base64. Node's permissive decoder silently discarded invalid input instead of surfacing the provider response as malformed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex image decoder now mirrors Codex's contract: trim surrounding Unicode White_Space, require the standard Base64 alphabet and canonical padding, and reject non-zero trailing bits before decoding. The existing encoded-size limit is preserved and other OpenAI image routes are unchanged. Compatibility risk is limited to malformed Codex image results; every input accepted by Codex's pinned strict decoder remains accepted here.

## User Impact

Malformed Codex image responses now fail with a clear provider-owned error instead of returning corrupted image bytes. Valid image responses continue to decode normally.

## Evidence

Current dependency contract check: Codex `origin/main` at [`0fb559f`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515) models the payload as the `result` string of an `image_generation_call` ([protocol model](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L987-L1006)). Both its image extension and core stream path call `result.trim()` and decode with `BASE64_STANDARD` ([image extension](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/ext/image-generation/src/tool.rs#L229-L239), [core stream path](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/core/src/stream_events_utils.rs#L109-L121)). Codex pins `base64` 0.22.1; that crate's `STANDARD` engine requires canonical padding, rejects non-zero trailing bits, and uses the standard alphabet ([configuration](https://github.com/marshallpierce/rust-base64/blob/v0.22.1/src/engine/general_purpose/mod.rs#L251-L263), [STANDARD engine](https://github.com/marshallpierce/rust-base64/blob/v0.22.1/src/engine/general_purpose/mod.rs#L331-L347)).

Direct inspection also found that OpenClaw's shared `canonicalizeBase64` intentionally accepts a wider set: internal ASCII whitespace and missing padding, and it does not reject non-zero trailing bits. The provider therefore uses that helper for bounded alphabet/padding normalization, then requires byte-for-byte canonical equality and validates the final unused bits. A committed positive regression covers U+0085 surrounding whitespace, which Rust `str::trim` accepts but JavaScript `trim()` does not. Negative regressions cover invalid alphabet characters in both terminal SSE shapes, missing padding, internal whitespace, and non-zero trailing bits.

Before/after behavior was exercised with a temporary local proof test that started a real `node:http` TCP server on `127.0.0.1`, returned Codex Responses SSE events, and called `buildOpenAIImageGenerationProvider().generateImage(...)` with private-network opt-in. Only auth resolution used a fixed `test-token`; the production provider, SSRF handling, HTTP request, bounded SSE reader/parser, decoder, and result construction were unchanged.

On current `upstream/main` before the patch, malformed `aGVs!bG8=` was accepted and silently decoded to `hello`:

```text
FAIL ... rejects malformed image data through real HTTP and SSE
AssertionError: promise resolved ... instead of rejecting
buffer data: [104, 101, 108, 108, 111]
Tests 1 failed | 1 skipped
```

With the patch, the same real HTTP/SSE proof rejected the malformed payload while its valid control decoded to `hello`:

```text
✓ rejects malformed image data through real HTTP and SSE 241ms
✓ accepts valid image data through real HTTP and SSE 5ms
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 2 passed (2)
```

Post-merge focused validation on the latest `upstream/main`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts packages/media-core/src/base64.test.ts
Test Files 2 passed (2)
Tests 82 passed (82)
```

Targeted `oxfmt --check`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` also passed. Full validation is running in GitHub Actions. Live OpenAI credentials were not available, so no request was sent to the hosted provider.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the source inspection and evidence above were run manually.
